title: Cottage cheese vs. ricotta: nutrition differences

seo.title: Cottage cheese vs. ricotta: protein and calories
seo.meta_description: Compare 2% cottage cheese and whole-milk ricotta per 100 g for calories, protein, fat and sodium. Cottage is leaner; ricotta is richer.
seo.search_intent: Compare cottage cheese and ricotta nutrition

excerpt: On an equal 100 g basis, a current 2% cottage cheese label works out to about 87 calories, 12.7 g protein and 2 g fat, while the current USDA whole-milk ricotta foundation reference provides 157 calories, 7.8 g protein and 11 g fat. Cottage is more protein-dense; ricotta is richer and lower in sodium in these references.
content_html:
Cottage cheese and ricotta are both soft white dairy products, yet they come from different cheesemaking traditions and behave differently nutritionally. Cottage is curd-based and moist; ricotta is traditionally a whey cheese and is usually richer.

Equal 100 g comparison

2% cottageWhole-milk ricotta
Calories~87157
Protein~12.7 g7.8 g
Fat~2.0 g11 g
Carbohydrate~3.3 g6.9 g
Sodium~347 mg~105 mg

The cottage example provides about 63% more protein by weight while containing roughly half the calories.

Why is ricotta richer?

Whole-milk ricotta contains much more fat. That creates the soft, creamy texture that works especially well in lasagna, stuffed pasta, cakes and desserts.

Cottage wins protein per calorie

At roughly 12.7 g protein for 87 calories, the cottage example is very efficient when protein is the goal. Ricotta offers about 7.8 g for 157 calories.

But cottage can be saltier

Good Culture 2% contains 520 mg sodium per 150 g, about 347 mg/100 g. The USDA ricotta reference is around 105 mg/100 g. This is a reminder that lower fat does not automatically mean lower sodium.

Can you substitute one for the other?

Sometimes, but texture changes. Cottage curds are more distinct and watery; ricotta is finer and richer. Blending cottage cheese can make it behave more like ricotta in some recipes, but the flavor and fat content remain different.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: The 2% cottage example: about 12.7 g/100 g versus 7.8 g in whole-milk ricotta.

faq.question: Which has more fat?
faq.answer: Ricotta: 11 g/100 g versus about 2 g in the cottage example.

faq.question: Which has more sodium?
faq.answer: The cottage example: roughly 347 mg/100 g versus about 105 mg in the USDA ricotta reference.
